name: Kamona Bijogo

earlier_scan.note: Only Koelle 1854 Polyglotta Africana wordlist and de Coutouly 1921 ethnographic note; Segerer's 2002 Bijogo grammar describes the Bubaque variety, not Kamona

readall_conflicts: No source states a stress rule for Kamona, so there is no placement disagreement. There is an identity disagreement over Koelle's data: Segerer 2000 (p. 12) identifies Koelle's two Bidsogo lists as Uno (262 terms; = list a, Ankaras, southern/Kajoko area) and Caraxe (258 terms; = list b, Wun, northern/Kamona area), whereas the clld/CLDF edition of Polyglotta Africana (Forkel et al. 2024's product) maps list a Ankaras to 'Bijogo-Kamona' (glottocode printed as kamo1253, sic) and list b Wun to 'Bijogo-Kajoko' (kajo1240), the opposite assignment. Glottolog attaches Koelle 1854 to kamo1256 without saying which list. Either way Koelle supplies accent marks, not a statement.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic note, no vocabulary. p.22-23: 'il faudrait le diviser en trois groupes distincts, parlant chacun un dialecte assez différent pour que les insulaires ne se comprennent pas entre eux' with group 1 = Caravellas, Caracho. Nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund W. 1854. Polyglotta Africana, or a comparative vocabulary of nearly three hundred words and phrases in more than one hundred distinct African languages. London: Church Missionary House. Bidsogo lists XII.A.a.2a (Ankaras) and 2b ('island Wun' = Caraxe per Segerer 2000:12)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only. Informant note: 'Bidsogo as spoken on the island Wun. From Aneyaoge, or Zacharias Macauly, of Kissy, born in the village of Kawun, on the island of Wun'. Preface lists among the marks employed 'the common sign for the accent', so accent is marked on individual items (scanned shows e.g. 'méngue, pl. béngiie'), but there is no statement of where accent falls.
